title: Sherlock Holmes: The Speckled Band
author: d'après Arthur Conan Doyle
desc: Une jeune femme terrifiée, un sifflement dans la nuit, et la mort mystérieuse de sa sœur.

p: One early morning in April 1883, Sherlock Holmes woke me up. "Sorry, Watson. A young lady is here. She is very frightened."
The lady was dressed in black. Her name was Helen Stoner. She was only thirty, but her hair was already turning grey.

"Two years ago, my twin sister Julia died," she said. "We lived with our stepfather, Dr. Grimesby Roylott, in an old house in Surrey. He is a violent man. He keeps wild animals from India in the garden: a cheetah and a baboon."
"How did your sister die?" asked Holmes.

"Two weeks before her wedding, she came to my room in the night. She was screaming. 'Helen! It was the band! The speckled band!' Then she fell and died. The doctors found nothing. No poison, no wound."
"Did you hear anything that night?" asked Holmes.
"Yes. A low whistle. And then a metal sound. Julia said she heard the whistle every night at three o'clock."
"And why are you here today?"
Helen's voice shook. "I am going to be married too. My stepfather is repairing my bedroom wall, so I must sleep in Julia's old room. And last night… I heard the whistle."

After she left, Dr. Roylott himself came to Baker Street. He was a huge, angry man. "Stay out of my business, Holmes!" He took the iron poker from the fireplace and bent it with his hands. Then he left.
Holmes calmly straightened the poker. "Watson, we go to Surrey today. And bring your revolver."
At the house, Holmes examined Julia's room carefully. He found three strange things.
First, a bell rope hung above the bed. But it was not connected to any bell. It was fake.
Second, there was a small ventilator in the wall. It did not go outside. It went into Dr. Roylott's room.
Third, the bed was fixed to the floor. It could not move.
In Dr. Roylott's room, Holmes found a metal safe, a saucer of milk, and a small dog leash tied in a loop.
"A saucer of milk," said Holmes quietly. "But there is no cat in this house, Watson."
He looked very serious. "Miss Stoner, tonight you must sleep in your own room. Watson and I will stay in your sister's room."
Holmes and I waited in the dark for hours. We didn't speak. At three o'clock, we saw a little light in the ventilator. Then we heard a soft, hissing sound.
Holmes jumped up, lit a match and hit the bell rope hard with his cane. "You see it, Watson? You see it?"
Then we heard a horrible scream from the next room.
We ran into Dr. Roylott's room. He was sitting on a chair, dead. Around his head, there was a strange yellow band with brown spots.
"The speckled band!" said Holmes. "A swamp adder, the most deadly snake in India!"

Roylott sent the snake through the ventilator, down the fake rope, to the bed. The milk and the whistle were to call it back. He wanted the girls' money. But when Holmes hit the snake, it went back angry — and bit its master.
"Violence, Watson," said Holmes, "always comes back to the violent."
